summary: Per-state percentile ranks and the required ordered result both depend on sorting arbitrary scores and identifiers, matching the window-ranking query's comparison-sort bound.

optimality.argument: Determining exact score ranks for arbitrary values and returning the selected rows under three ordering keys requires comparison ordering in the general case; partitioned windows and the final order run within O(n log n).

replacement_checks.evidence: Arbitrary per-state scores determine exact top-five-percent rank boundaries and boundary ties.
Partitioned rank and count windows plus one final result sort execute in O(n log n).
Cases cover singleton states, twenty and twenty-one row cutoffs, ceiling, maximum and boundary ties, partition isolation, and all output keys.
